scope: Source-bound review of the existing Knowledge Document against the reading copy accepted for text assessment, covering identity, research question, method, findings, limitations, literal quotations and their locators, controlled-category relevance and the figure values the reading copy now carries. The reviewer did not author the document and does not author the requested changes, so the rebinding waits for a revision by a producer other than this reviewer and a fresh review. This receipt grants no human verification, promotion or publication authority.

findings.finding: The reading copy is arXiv revision 2406.12033v2 with the same title and seven authors, and its body preserves every identity-bound line. All three displayed quotations resolve exactly once in the reading copy, at reading-copy lines 54 (section 1, under a Docling-promoted warning heading), 291 (section 4.5) and 320 (section 5); their locators hold.

findings.location: Research question and method; Main findings
findings.finding: The document twice names the fairness metric as equality of opportunity ('equality-of-opportunity differences', 'balance between classification performance and equality of opportunity'). Section 3.5 uses Equalized Odds, which requires similar true-positive and false-positive rates across groups and is computed as their standard deviation for multi-class factors; equality of opportunity constrains true-positive rates only. Replace both with equalized odds (EO).

After rebinding to the reading copy, the sentences 'Conversion QC remained incomplete during preparation, and figures were not independently inspected. This distillate therefore omits table- and figure-dependent numerical comparisons.' no longer describe the bound representation. Independent conversion QC accepted the reading copy for text assessment, with Figure 1 described and the Figure 2 and 3 values recomputed from the vector geometry. As in the J4K3XA52 precedent, the Limitations paragraph and the source-representation boundary must state the accepted repair and its remaining limits (figure values are plot readings, not author tables, no figure graphics attached) before the binding changes.

'sixty variants across seven social factors and their combinations' miscounts the design. Sections 1 and 3.2 name six single factors (gender, race, age, religion, sexuality, nationality) plus their combinations as the seventh, with 24 expert-proposed combinations among the 60 variants. The document also omits the four BERT-based discriminative baselines (BERT, RoBERTa, MentalBERT, MentalRoBERTa) beside the ten LLMs, although its main findings compare LLMs with 'smaller domain-specific encoders'.

'Demographic enrichment inserts synthetic identity context and may not represent how demographic information appears in practice' is not stated by the authors. Section 6 says the enrichment may not capture the diverse biases of LLMs because it focuses on demographic bias. Either align the sentence with section 6 or mark it as the document's own inference.

The Figure 2 values of the reading copy support the hedged association of scale with better aggregate results: the three smallest LLMs average 47.0 to 47.9 F1 and 35.5 to 38.8 EO, GPT-4 66.2 F1 and 23.9 EO. The relation is not monotonic (Gemma-7B 58.4 F1 above Llama2-13B 55.1, Llama3-8B EO 30.2 above Llama2-7B 26.0), and MentalRoBERTa (70.1 F1, 17.8 EO) exceeds every LLM, which supports the statement that general LLMs did not uniformly outperform domain-specific encoders.

findings.location: Core statement s3 and Main findings, prompting
findings.finding: Table 4 supports s3: each of the four fairness-aware prompts lowers EO against the reference row in all nine model-dataset cells, and FC gives the lowest EO in each. The reference rows mix zero-shot SP (Gemma-2B) and few-shot CoT results (Llama3-8B, GPT-4, matching Table 2), which the document does not overstate. Few-shot CoT raises EO in several Table 2 cells (for example GPT-4 on SWMH 10.5 to 12.3, Llama3-8B on MultiWD 30.3 to 32.5), so the hedge 'in several evaluated settings' is necessary and should stay.

findings.location: Stratified results not used by the document
findings.finding: Sections 4.3 and 5 state that the models struggle more with religion and nationality. The Figure 3 values of the reading copy show nationality with the highest average F1 for all four models and no highest EO for any model, while religion has the lowest F1 for Gemma-2B and Llama3-8B and the highest EO for Gemma-2B and GPT-4. The document does not adopt the claim; a revision that adds stratified findings must record this tension rather than repeat the authors' wording.

Generative_KI, Prompting, Bias_Ungleichheit, Diversitaet and Fairness remain central, Gender is supported as one evaluated factor and part of combinations such as 'Black female youth'. Soziale_Arbeit, AI_Literacies and Feministisch are correctly excluded. The figure values change none of these assignments.
